meta.title: Introduction
meta.description: Bevel UI ships fully-engineered UI systems — not component libraries. Each system solves a complete, hard UI engineering problem so you can drop in working architecture rather than build it from scratch.

blocks.content: A component library gives you a button. Bevel gives you the entire multi-step form — state machine, per-step validation, back/forward navigation, error recovery, progress persistence. Every edge case already handled. Every architectural decision already made.
Bevel is built on the same foundation as shadcn/ui — you copy the source code into your project and own it forever. No npm package to upgrade. No breaking changes forced on you. No lock-in.

steps.title: Install a system
steps.description: Use the shadcn CLI to copy the system files into your project.

steps.title: Drop it in
steps.description: Import from your local components folder — the same path the CLI installed to.

steps.title: Own it forever
steps.description: The code lives in your project. Style it, extend it, fork it. It's yours.

blocks.content: Three principles guide every system in Bevel.

blocks.title: No installs
blocks.content: Copy the source directly into your project. No npm package to upgrade.

blocks.title: No lock-in
blocks.content: You own the code. Change anything. Style it however you want.

blocks.title: Solve the hard problem
blocks.content: Every system ships with the architecture already figured out. State machine, edge cases, accessibility, keyboard navigation — all included.

blocks.title: Is this a component library?
blocks.content: No. A component library gives you primitives like buttons and inputs. Bevel gives you complete systems — Product Tour, Command Palette, File Upload, Form Engine. These are solutions to hard UI engineering problems, not building blocks.

blocks.title: Can I use it with my existing shadcn/ui setup?
blocks.content: Yes. Bevel is built on top of shadcn/ui primitives. It uses the same Button, Input, Badge, Dialog components you already have.

blocks.title: Does it work with React 19?
blocks.content: Yes. Every system is built with React 18+ in mind and is compatible with React 19.

blocks.title: Do I need Tailwind CSS?
blocks.content: Yes. Bevel uses Tailwind CSS v4 for all styling. If you're using shadcn/ui you already have Tailwind set up.
